title#en: Strengthening the Health Resilience of Communities Vulnerable to Climate Change in Benin’s ABD (Adjohoun, Bonou and Dangbo) Zone
title#fr: Strengthening the Health Resilience of Communities Vulnerable to Climate Change in Benin’s ABD (Adjohoun, Bonou and Dangbo) Zone
title#es: Strengthening the Health Resilience of Communities Vulnerable to Climate Change in Benin’s ABD (Adjohoun, Bonou and Dangbo) Zone
title#pt: Strengthening the Health Resilience of Communities Vulnerable to Climate Change in Benin’s ABD (Adjohoun, Bonou and Dangbo) Zone
description#en: Benin, particularly the Adjohoun, Bonou, and Dangbo (ABD) zone in the Ouémé department, faces significant exposure to climate change impacts, including increasing temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and extreme events such as floods, and extreme heat which exacerbate climate-sensitive diseases. This project, building on Benin’s national strategies for climate adaptation and health system strengthening, targets the ABD zone to enhance the climate resilience of vulnerable communities and local health systems. The area is experiencing increasing incidence of floods, vector-borne disease outbreaks, and infrastructure vulnerability, disproportionately affecting poor households, women, and children under five. The initiative directly benefits approximately 97,900 people and indirectly benefits an additional 213,800 by establishing a community-based climate-health Early Warning System (EWS), upgrading climate-resilient health facilities, and promoting sustainable community adaptation measures. The project focuses on strengthening the enabling environment for integrating climate information into health service delivery, investing in resilient water, sanitation, and energy infrastructure for health centres, and promoting nature-based solutions and traditional medicine gardens to safeguard livelihoods. The project comprises three components aligned with the Green Climate Fund’s 2024–2027 Strategic Plan. Component 1 will establish local EWS capacity and climate-health risk monitoring, integrating climate forecasts with disease surveillance and response. Component 2 focuses on implementing concrete adaptation measures, including renewable energy for health facilities, improved WASH services, and resilient transport solutions during floods. Component 3 supports capacity building for health workers and communities to plan and respond effectively to climate-health risks. GCF funding is essential given Benin’s status as a Least Developed Country with constrained public health financing and limited donor focus on health system adaptation. The project aims to position the ABD zone as a model for integrated climate-health resilience planning and action in Benin.

LGCC3 Project structure

 

20. Capacitation of Districts and communities to respond, plan and budget for
gender inclusive climate change adaptation




Expected Outcome 1: Institutional and community climate adaptation capacity is
strengthened and embedded into local plans and budgets aligned with national
climate priorities and social inclusion.




Expected Result 1: Awareness and capacity are built-in selected local
communities to respond to climate change adaptation.

Capacity development activities of local administrators and community actors
will support mainstreaming of gender and socially inclusive climate change
adaptation responses in alignment with the NP-SNDD in selected Districts.
The Districts will be selected based on results from the Climate Risk Assessment
(CRA) undertaken during the PPF phase and relate to rural community
vulnerability especially related to floods and droughts and agriculture and
water resource sectors. Project Result 1 is led by NCDDS with technical
assistance from UNCDF including support NCDDS addressing information and
institutional barriers, in addition to developing gender-sensitive knowledge
products supportive of EDA project results for inter-District awareness,
advocacy and expansion. Building the capacity of the initial selected Districts
in climate change adaptation risks, impacts and responses will develop a strong
foundation for locally-led adaptation which enables these Districts to be
attractive and receptive to potential investors identified later in the Project
during Project Result 4 activities. A mixture of gender inclusive traditional
training, e-learning and professional development support will be developed by
UNCDF and provided for key District and Commune Administrators and local
community members (with face-to-face trainings being compliant with local
epidemic/COVID pandemic measures at the time). With UNCDF Technical Assistance,
the awareness and capacity interventions will be developed based on identified
needs of local stakeholders from a gap analysis. The organization of these
capacity development activities such training will be conducted by NCDDs.
Success of the training effectiveness will be evaluated through a mainstreaming
index which will be used for systemizing training to other Districts for
scaling-up under Outcome 2.




Activities:

 * concept note on the role of local government and local actors on
   mainstreaming CCA under the framework of the National Programme 2 (NP2);
 * training needs assessment and gap analysis on climate awareness inclusive of
   gender;
 * gender inclusive course development for capacity building on localized
   climate adaptation response, mainstreamed into selected Districts;
 * effectiveness of capacity building will be monitored using a CCA
   mainstreaming index which forms part of the Annual Performance Assessment
   (APA);
 * gender inclusive knowledge products developed and shared across Cambodia’s
   Districts through web content, audio-visual and printed documents, Further
   sharing of knowledge products through the wider LoCAL network.

 

Expected Result 2: Locally-led risk-informed climate adaptation planning and
budgeting is embedded into at least 15 Districts.

At least 15 Districts that mainstreamed climate adaptation responses in Project
Result 1, will be supported to develop gender inclusive Enhanced District
Climate Change Strategies (EDCCS) that embed the new PBCRG process. UNCDF will
provide Technical Assistance to NCDD to develop these new high-level strategies
to address the technical barrier for integration of localized climate risk data
and selection of high priority target Communes and sub-projects within the
Districts, and importantly the embedding of new processes that build-in the
PBCRG, within existing government systems for planning and budgeting. The EDCCS
includes: (1) GIS mapping of soils, hydrology, agriculture production, known
climate risks.; (2) analysis of meteorological data and predicted future trends;
(3) participatory vulnerability reduction analysis;(4) key climate
vulnerabilities (communities, locations, sectors, infrastructure, ecosystems);
(5) response strategies; and (6) multi-year sub-projects targeting the most
vulnerable communities. The purpose of the EDCCS is to enable optimal selection
of scientifically evidenced investments for climate resilience. The EDCCS will
be integrated in the District Development Plan and three-year rolling District
Investment Programme by NCDDS and will be of value in climate-proofing all
investments undertaken by the District Administration and by the Commune
Councils within the District. This creates the fundamental change required for
an institutionalised shift that will be demonstrated under Project Result 3 and
support expansion under Project Result 4.

 

Activities:

 * collect local risk-informed climate data;
 * gender inclusive Enhanced District Climate Change Strategies (EDCCS) –
   including the identification of target Communes within vulnerable Districts
   and sub-projects, and the embedding of gender inclusive climate adaptation
   planning and budgeting systems;
 * support NCDDS with M&E and compliance-based reporting.




21. On-granting of PBCRG and leveraging of national climate adaptation funding




Expected Outcome 2: Local governments nationally have access to sustainable
climate adaptation funding leveraged by national priorities e.g. NP2, SCF (a
Sub-national Climate Fund which forms a current GCF Readiness Proposal submitted
and managed by the NCDD-S).), and SNIF (Sub-National Investment Fund and managed
by the Ministry of Economic and Finance: MEF).




Expected Result 3: Climate resilient investments are implemented through the
PBCRG system and 15 District Investment Programmes.




Project Result 3 is led by NCDD-S to address institutional barriers through
establishing a national PBCRG Board and Framework and implementing the EDCCS in
the 15 target districts with technical assistance from UNCDF. This ensures
District Investment Programmes (DIPs) select PBCRG eligible sub-projects that
are submitted to the PBCRG Board for consideration on meeting minimum conditions
followed by allocation of the climate-specific grant. PBCRG grant cycles will be
implemented along with Annual Performance Assessments where UNCDF will provide
Quality Assurance in this process as part of a results-based performance model
that aligns with project impact and continued improvement of climate change
adaptation investments at the District level. Result 3 focuses on systematizing
climate-specific on-granting through the institutionalized EDCCS and associated
planning (embedded through the District Development Plan) and budgeting
(embedded through the DIP) systems. Therefore, existing District government
systems are enhanced to formally integrate local climate change adaptation
investments.




Activities:

 * National gender-balanced PBCRG Board is established, and PBCRG Framework
   approved;
 * Districts implement EDCCS through the gender-inclusive District Investment
   Programme;
 * District PBCRGs selected in line with eligibility criteria and minimum
   conditions. Based on an indication of the PBCRG allocation (grant allocations
   formulation will be included in the feasibility study under PPF), the
   Districts will integrate the sub-projects in their annual budgets which are
   approved by the District Administrations. The Districts will implement
   through their budget execution processes;
 * Cycles of grant allocations approved and transferred;
 * Annual Performance Assessments conducted in 15 Districts.

 

Expected Result 4: An effective PBCRG (finance mechanism) is deployed across
Cambodia and operational for additional funding.

 

Project Result 4 is led by NCDD-S and addresses financial barriers to enable
continued and expanded use of the PBCRG post-project. The National PBCRG
Scale-up Strategy includes results from the Cost-Benefit-Analysis (CBA)
undertaken under the Cambodia Readiness Project focused on operationalizing a
Sub-National Climate Fund (SCF) managed by the NCDD-S. Hence the National
Scale-up Strategy identifies current and future potential public and private
sources, amounts and windows of climate financing earmarked for District and
Commune level investment in Cambodia, implemented through the District
Administration, in addition to plans for how to engage those funders. UNCDF will
provide Technical Assistance to NCDD on the integration of CBA to the PBCRGs in
Cambodia. Additional to the 15 Districts with institutionalized PBCRG systems,
are the potential Districts that mainstreamed climate change adaptation
responses under Project Result 1 that are essentially ready for EDCCS
development and implementation as part of the next cohort in the scale-up
strategy. The scaling-up stage is complemented by national and international
dialogues with potential partners and parallel financing opportunities. Further
to this, regulatory enhancement through NP2 resulting in recapitalization and
funding facilities such as the SCF and the SNIF, will support these efforts to
scale the PBCRG across Cambodia. The PBCRG Framework, which UNCDF will provide
technical assistance to update the design and related annexes, will guide the
final development of the PBCRG design and Manual to standardize and
operationalize the PBCRG system, while scaling-up District and Commune level
administrative capacities in on-going planning and budgeting for climate change
adaptation investments. The capture of gender inclusive lessons learned support
continued scale-up efforts through knowledge management, sharing and advocacy
for sub-national climate investment.

 

Activities:

 * National PBCRG scale-up strategy developed, including the next new batch of
   PBCRG-ready Districts, which will be identified during PPF. 
 * the integration of the results from the Cost-Benefit-Analysis market/private
   sector landscape study from the GCF Readiness Proposal “A Framework and
   Manual to launch a Sub-national Climate Fund (SCF) aligned with LoCAL in
   Cambodia”;
 * PBCRG design, manual and tools refined (inclusive of gender perspectives)
 * NCDD-S monitoring of PBCRG activities for implementation;
 * Gender inclusive lessons learned captured and used for awareness, advocacy
   and expansion.

potential for transformation. Has it been piloted in the country or region? Are
the proposed interventions well documented for their costs and benefits?




22 Readiness for scaling-up

The EDA project of LGCC3 is ready for scaling-up following success from previous
Phase I and II LGCC results (see below), and will enable at least 15 targeted
Districts to strengthen their response to identified climate risks and impacts,
by reducing vulnerabilities through climate risk-informed investments for
climate adaptation. The success of the 15 Districts in institutionalizing and
systematizing local climate change adaptation planning and budgeting combined
with a National climate specific Performance-Based Climate Resilience Grant
(PBCRG) Scale-up Strategy will position Cambodia to expand the program to more
Districts. This may include the next 50 Districts earmarked (to be confirmed
after PPF) and ready to develop and embed the EDCCS based on the capacity
building and mainstreaming efforts delivered in LGCC3 under Project Result 1.




The National Scale-Up Strategy will be complemented by efforts to harness
parallel financing from potential partners and national resources under policies
and funding facilities such as NP2, SCF and SNIF.

. From a technical standpoint, local capacities, and knowledge particularly
those of the NCDD-S and other Steering Group and PMU stakeholders have
significantly increased during the past 10-years since LoCAL was established in
Cambodia. This has resulted in a stronger enabling environment receptive to a
scale-up of the PBCRG as part of LGCC3 and an overall transformational change.




23. EDA project selection criteria for sub-project PBCRG investments

Under LGCC3 the pre-financing PBCRG will be transferred to the District
Administration upon meeting minimum standards. The PBCRG is managed and
monitored by the NCDD-S, and overseen by a Grants Committee, which requires the
District to plan and budget for a menu of eligible local climate risk-informed
investments, or sub-projects. The menu of eligible investments for sub-projects
will be refined during the PPF phase after the Climate Vulnerability Assessment
and Feasibility Study have been conducted. An example of a menu of investments
and indicative costings for adaptation interventions aligned with the climate
specific PBCRG is provided in Annex 3. Each of the targeted 15 Districts in the
LGCC3 project will develop an ‘Enhanced District Climate Change Strategy’
(EDCCS) aligned with a ‘District Investment Programme’ (DIP) to identify local
context-specific climate risks, vulnerable groups, locations and key adaptation
measures by intervention area, specific sub-project type, and size. The NCDD-S
will indicate to the District Administration, to take into account a PBCRG award
when developing its annual plans and budget. Therefore, the District
Administration’s budget will reflect its existing budget commitments to climate
response and the PBCRG transfer for eligible climate-subprojects. The PBCRG for
sub-projects focus on climate-specific standalone funding and top-up existing
District Administration allocations towards resilient and sustainable
development. The PBCRG is therefore ringfenced and traceable through District
planning and budgeting cycles.




24. Eligible District investments areas aim to respond directly to the GCF’s
four climate change adaptation result areas (see Annex 3: Menu of Eligible
investment):

1. Services for strengthening the climate resilience of vulnerable people,
communities and livelihoods (including planning and capacity building);

2. Services for strengthening climate resilience for health, water and food
security;

3. Climate proofing of infrastructure to protect against climate-related damage
and support adaptation (incremental cost); and

4. Ecosystems and ecosystem services.




25. The PBCRG directly supports the District’s capacity, planning,
decision-making, budgeting and implementation of local adaptation measures in
order to reduce their vulnerability to climate change impacts. The performance
of the pre-financing climate-specific PBCRG is subject to an Annual Performance
Assessment (APA) 12-months following disbursement, with the results affecting
future grant levels to the District Administration. The PBCRG therefore offers
additionality and an incentive for good performance at the local government
level.







26. The PBCRG mechanism, see Figure 10, follows a successfully tested process
adopted as part of the LoCAL facility in 14 other countries, first piloted in
Cambodia and Bhutan in 2011 (see Annex 4 for LoCAL background). The
operationalization of the PBCRG in Cambodia will follow the specific operational
and approval steps outlined in Annex 4.




[data:image/png;base64,]

Figure 10: The PBCRG cycle




27. Pilot testing in Cambodia: The Local Climate Adaptive Living (LoCAL)
Facility of UNCDF is recognized by the LDC Expert Group (LEG) as a standard
mechanism to channel climate finance to local governments meeting EDA
requirements of devolved decision-making and locally-led climate action.
Cambodia implementation of LoCAL includes:

 

Phase I Testing: 3 Districts in the Takeo Province: the Doun Kaev Municipality
and the Bati and Bourei Cholsar Districts. Funds supported from CCCA Trust Fund
and UNCDF. Total funding amounted USD164,686

Phase II Consolidating: 5 Districts in Battambang: Bavel, Moung Russei, Rokha
Kiri, Sampov Loun and Thma Koul. The funding for this LGGC2 and Bridging phase
amounts to USD1.6 Million from SIDA and UNCDF.

Phase III Systematizing: LGCC3 targets at least 15 of the most vulnerable
Districts in Cambodia. Funds from GCF, UNCDF and Districts.




28. LGCC3, therefore, represents systematizing of the LoCAL model, following
successful results from Phase I and II including 2 Districts and 1 municipality
in Takeo province, 5 Districts in Battambang province, 276 adaptive measures
financed, the integration of climate change and disaster risk management into
sub-national planning and budgeting, on average 85% of PBCRG’s invested in
climate adaptive measures and overall 51% of female beneficiaries accessed PBCRG
investments. Of the total investments made, 229 represented small-scale
infrastructure projects mainly entailing construction of elevated roads/bridges
and renovation/construction of rural/farm roads; restoration/protection of
irrigation canals; and rehabilitation/construction of water gates, sewage
systems, and community ponds. These types of investments are indicatively
provided in Annex 3, would be potential sub-projects for financing in LGCC3.




29. Lessons learned from the earlier phases to be addressed and integrated into
Phase III through LGCC3 include:

 * Local governments have adequate capacity for simple climate change response
   actions but further capacity development is needed.
 * Smarter systems are needed to facilitate scale-up, and more cross sector
   partnerships are needed.
 * Access to accurate and reliable data, involvement from District and local
   communities is key to ensure adaptation results at the local level.
 * An innovative approach like PBCRG requires long-term policy support. To
   facilitate this, advocacy and knowledge sharing is needed from policy-makers
   with evidence from the field.




30. These and other results are provided in the Final Assessment report (2020)
“Cambodia’s Local Governments and Climate Change Project Bridging Phase”, and
the (2018) “Financing local adaptation to climate change: PBCRG experiences and
results are provided as an attachment to this Concept Note. In addition to the
web resource: https://www.uncdf.org/local/cambodia. The interventions eligible
for PBCRG finance are of proven effectiveness and data on costs and benefits are
available. Annex 3 on the menu of potential PBCRG climate sub-project
investments shares indicative costs for resilient interventions based on GCF
result areas. In addition, results from cost-benefit-analysis studies by the
Asian Development Bank on the cost of health benefits from small-scale water
interventions on rural livelihoods and returns on investment from climate
proofing small-scale infrastructure, have been shown to be positive. A
cost-benefit analysis for LGCC3 will be developed at the Feasibility Study stage
to be conducted at the PPF Service phase.




31. At scale, the LoCAL mechanism has transformative potential as seen in other
applications such as Bhutan which started in 2 Districts and has now scaled to
100 in Phase II. In Cambodia this transformative capacity will enable local
governments to develop science-based adaptation strategies, mainstream
resilience in their plans and budgets and invest to build resilience in
communities that lack the resources needed to adapt independently, in alignment
with EDA approaches for locally-led adaptation. To some extent this has already
been evidenced in Cambodia by a successful transition from Phase I to phase II
with good prospects for Phase III. The PBCRG, as a single standalone
climate-specific facility has clearly impacted the local climate response
landscape in Cambodia and has potential to service more Districts, as evidenced
by recent replication efforts with partners such as IFAD’s GEF- ASPIRE
(Agriculture Services Programme for Innovation, Resilience and Extension) and
Sustainable Resilient Livelihoods (SRL) programme, a UNDP programme.

 

 

PBCRG Process

 

32. As outlined in Annex 4, specific PBCRG requirements must be complied with by
the District as part of the approvals process. A PBCRG will be allocated to
eligible Districts based on set eligibility criteria outlined earlier. Grant
awards will be calculated using a 75% base allocation, 25% population allocation
and 25% APA score allocation. PBCRG Minimum Conditions (MC) thresholds include:
a) for first year access: the District has established a Climate Change Working
Group under the leadership of the Board of Governors; b) for second year access:
additional to first year MC, Council approval of the EDCCS; and c) for
subsequent years access additional to first and second year MC, a minimum
acceptable CCA Mainstreaming Index score. Sub-project proposals will be screened
by the Grants Committee (which is overseen by an Audit and Ethics Committee),
for eligibility. Eligible expenditure with PBCRG funds include: (1) preparation
of EDCCS; (2) design of sub-projects to build resilience of identified highly
climate-vulnerable groups and communities; and (3) sub-projects. Sub-projects
will address GCF adaptation strategic impact Area 1: Climate resilience of
livelihoods; Area 2: health, food and water security, including emergency and
disaster preparedness; Area 3: climate-proofing critical infrastructure
(incremental costs); and Area 4: climate resilient ecosystems and ecosystem
services. The EDCCS will be integrated in the District Development Plan and
three-year rolling District Investment Programme and will be of value in
climate-proofing all investments undertaken by the District Administration and
by the Commune Councils within the District. Performance measures with equal
weighting include: (1) quality of PBCRG outputs; (2) quality of PBCRG
implementation process; (3) number, targeting of most vulnerable groups and
participatory evaluation by the beneficiaries; and (4) Climate Change
Mainstreaming Index. An independent assessor will be contracted for the Annual
Performance Appraisal and results will be presented in an annual reflection
workshop. The Districts will be encouraged to prepare self-capacity development
plans based on weaknesses identified.




Describe in what way the Accredited Entity(ies) is well placed to undertake the
planned activities and what the implementation arrangements with the executing
entity(ies) and implementing partners will be.

 

 

Implementation Arrangement




33. See Figure 12 below for proposed project implementation arrangements and
Figure 13 for the suggested flow of funds for the project. A Steering Committee
will oversee implementation, with the NCDDS as the Accredited Entity, as the
lead implementing agency for LGCC3. NCDD-S will therefore report directly to the
GCF Board for the overall management of LGCC3, as well as for the financial,
monitoring and reporting aspects of the EDA project activities.




Where NCDDS under its Project Management and Support Division (PMSD) will be
responsible for all Components, the District administrations will implement the
sub-projects and UNCDF will provide advisory, Technical Assistance and Quality
Assurance to all Components (20% of the project will be implemented with direct
support of UNCDF). 




The District Administration will comply with the PBCRG process, implement
investments and manage the implementation of works and services associated with
sub-projects and sub-grants to local Commune Councils.

23. EDA project selection criteria for sub-project PBCRG investments

Under LGCC3 the pre-financing PBCRG will be transferred to the District
Administration upon meeting minimum standards. The PBCRG is managed and
monitored by the NCDD-S, and overseen by a Grants Committee, which requires the
District to plan and budget for a menu of eligible local climate risk-informed
investments, or sub-projects. The menu of eligible investments for sub-projects
will be refined during the PPF phase after the Climate Vulnerability Assessment
and Feasibility Study have been conducted. An example of a menu of investments
and indicative costings for adaptation interventions aligned with the climate
specific PBCRG is provided in Annex 3. Each of the targeted 15 Districts in the
LGCC3 project will develop an ‘Enhanced District Climate Change Strategy’
(EDCCS) aligned with a ‘District Investment Programme’ (DIP) to identify local
context-specific climate risks, vulnerable groups, locations and key adaptation
measures by intervention area, specific sub-project type, and size. The NCDD-S
will indicate to the District Administration, to take into account a PBCRG award
when developing its annual plans and budget. Therefore, the District
Administration’s budget will reflect its existing budget commitments to climate
response and the PBCRG transfer for eligible climate-subprojects. The PBCRG for
sub-projects focus on climate-specific standalone funding and top-up existing
District Administration allocations towards resilient and sustainable
development. The PBCRG is therefore ringfenced and traceable through District
planning and budgeting cycles.




24. Eligible District investments areas aim to respond directly to the GCF’s
four climate change adaptation result areas (see Annex 3: Menu of Eligible
investment):

1. Services for strengthening the climate resilience of vulnerable people,
communities and livelihoods (including planning and capacity building);

2. Services for strengthening climate resilience for health, water and food
security;

3. Climate proofing of infrastructure to protect against climate-related damage
and support adaptation (incremental cost); and

4. Ecosystems and ecosystem services.




25. The PBCRG directly supports the District’s capacity, planning,
decision-making, budgeting and implementation of local adaptation measures in
order to reduce their vulnerability to climate change impacts. The performance
of the pre-financing climate-specific PBCRG is subject to an Annual Performance
Assessment (APA) 12-months following disbursement, with the results affecting
future grant levels to the District Administration. The PBCRG therefore offers
additionality and an incentive for good performance at the local government
level.







26. The PBCRG mechanism, see Figure 10, follows a successfully tested process
adopted as part of the LoCAL facility in 14 other countries, first piloted in
Cambodia and Bhutan in 2011 (see Annex 4 for LoCAL background). The
operationalization of the PBCRG in Cambodia will follow the specific operational
and approval steps outlined in Annex 4.

27. Pilot testing in Cambodia: The Local Climate Adaptive Living (LoCAL)
Facility of UNCDF is recognized by the LDC Expert Group (LEG) as a standard
mechanism to channel climate finance to local governments meeting EDA
requirements of devolved decision-making and locally-led climate action.
Cambodia implementation of LoCAL includes:

 

Phase I Testing: 3 Districts in the Takeo Province: the Doun Kaev Municipality
and the Bati and Bourei Cholsar Districts. Funds supported from CCCA Trust Fund
and UNCDF. Total funding amounted USD164,686

Phase II Consolidating: 5 Districts in Battambang: Bavel, Moung Russei, Rokha
Kiri, Sampov Loun and Thma Koul. The funding for this LGGC2 and Bridging phase
amounts to USD1.6 Million from SIDA and UNCDF.

Districts in Cambodia. Funds from GCF, UNCDF and Districts.




28. LGCC3, therefore, represents systematizing of the LoCAL model, following
successful results from Phase I and II including 2 Districts and 1 municipality
in Takeo province, 5 Districts in Battambang province, 276 adaptive measures
financed, the integration of climate change and disaster risk management into
sub-national planning and budgeting, on average 85% of PBCRG’s invested in
climate adaptive measures and overall 51% of female beneficiaries accessed PBCRG
investments. Of the total investments made, 229 represented small-scale
infrastructure projects mainly entailing construction of elevated roads/bridges
and renovation/construction of rural/farm roads; restoration/protection of
irrigation canals; and rehabilitation/construction of water gates, sewage
systems, and community ponds. These types of investments are indicatively
provided in Annex 3, would be potential sub-projects for financing in LGCC3.

Phase III through LGCC3 include:

   partnerships are needed.

   communities is key to ensure adaptation results at the local level.

   facilitate this, advocacy and knowledge sharing is needed from policy-makers
   with evidence from the field.

applications such as Bhutan which started in 2 Districts and has now scaled to

governments to develop science-based adaptation strategies, mainstream
resilience in their plans and budgets and invest to build resilience in

PBCRG Process

 

32. As outlined in Annex 4, specific PBCRG requirements must be complied with by
the District as part of the approvals process. A PBCRG will be allocated to
eligible Districts based on set eligibility criteria outlined earlier. Grant
awards will be calculated using a 75% base allocation, 25% population allocation
and 25% APA score allocation. PBCRG Minimum Conditions (MC) thresholds include:
a) for first year access: the District has established a Climate Change Working
Group under the leadership of the Board of Governors; b) for second year access:
additional to first year MC, Council approval of the EDCCS; and c) for
subsequent years access additional to first and second year MC, a minimum
acceptable CCA Mainstreaming Index score. Sub-project proposals will be screened
by the Grants Committee (which is overseen by an Audit and Ethics Committee),

of EDCCS; (2) design of sub-projects to build resilience of identified highly
climate-vulnerable groups and communities; and (3) sub-projects. Sub-projects
will address GCF adaptation strategic impact Area 1: Climate resilience of
livelihoods; Area 2: health, food and water security, including emergency and
disaster preparedness; Area 3: climate-proofing critical infrastructure
(incremental costs); and Area 4: climate resilient ecosystems and ecosystem
services. The EDCCS will be integrated in the District Development Plan and
three-year rolling District Investment Programme and will be of value in
climate-proofing all investments undertaken by the District Administration and
by the Commune Councils within the District. Performance measures with equal
weighting include: (1) quality of PBCRG outputs; (2) quality of PBCRG

workshop. The Districts will be encouraged to prepare self-capacity development
plans based on weaknesses identified.

communities to respond to climate change adaptation.

will support mainstreaming of gender and socially inclusive climate change
adaptation responses in alignment with the NP-SNDD in selected Districts.

(CRA) undertaken during the PPF phase and relate to rural community
vulnerability especially related to floods and droughts and agriculture and
water resource sectors. Project Result 1 is led by NCDDS with technical
assistance from UNCDF including support NCDDS addressing information and
institutional barriers, in addition to developing gender-sensitive knowledge
products supportive of EDA project results for inter-District awareness,
advocacy and expansion. Building the capacity of the initial selected Districts
in climate change adaptation risks, impacts and responses will develop a strong
foundation for locally-led adaptation which enables these Districts to be
attractive and receptive to potential investors identified later in the Project
during Project Result 4 activities. A mixture of gender inclusive traditional
training, e-learning and professional development support will be developed by
UNCDF and provided for key District and Commune Administrators and local
community members (with face-to-face trainings being compliant with local
epidemic/COVID pandemic measures at the time). With UNCDF Technical Assistance,
the awareness and capacity interventions will be developed based on identified
needs of local stakeholders from a gap analysis. The organization of these
capacity development activities such training will be conducted by NCDDs.

index which will be used for systemizing training to other Districts for
scaling-up under Outcome 2.

   mainstreaming CCA under the framework of the National Programme 2 (NP2);

   climate adaptation response, mainstreamed into selected Districts;

   mainstreaming index which forms part of the Annual Performance Assessment
   (APA);
 * gender inclusive knowledge products developed and shared across Cambodia’s
   Districts through web content, audio-visual and printed documents, Further
   sharing of knowledge products through the wider LoCAL network.

budgeting is embedded into at least 15 Districts.

Result 1, will be supported to develop gender inclusive Enhanced District
Climate Change Strategies (EDCCS) that embed the new PBCRG process. UNCDF will
provide Technical Assistance to NCDD to develop these new high-level strategies
to address the technical barrier for integration of localized climate risk data
and selection of high priority target Communes and sub-projects within the
Districts, and importantly the embedding of new processes that build-in the
PBCRG, within existing government systems for planning and budgeting. The EDCCS
includes: (1) GIS mapping of soils, hydrology, agriculture production, known
climate risks.; (2) analysis of meteorological data and predicted future trends;
(3) participatory vulnerability reduction analysis;(4) key climate
vulnerabilities (communities, locations, sectors, infrastructure, ecosystems);
(5) response strategies; and (6) multi-year sub-projects targeting the most
vulnerable communities. The purpose of the EDCCS is to enable optimal selection
of scientifically evidenced investments for climate resilience. The EDCCS will
be integrated in the District Development Plan and three-year rolling District
Investment Programme by NCDDS and will be of value in climate-proofing all
investments undertaken by the District Administration and by the Commune
Councils within the District. This creates the fundamental change required for
an institutionalised shift that will be demonstrated under Project Result 3 and
support expansion under Project Result 4.

 * collect local risk-informed climate data;

   including the identification of target Communes within vulnerable Districts

   planning and budgeting systems;
 * support NCDDS with M&E and compliance-based reporting.

Phase I and II LGCC results (see below), and will enable at least 15 targeted
Districts to strengthen their response to identified climate risks and impacts,
by reducing vulnerabilities through climate risk-informed investments for
climate adaptation. The success of the 15 Districts in institutionalizing and
systematizing local climate change adaptation planning and budgeting combined
with a National climate specific Performance-Based Climate Resilience Grant
(PBCRG) Scale-up Strategy will position Cambodia to expand the program to more
Districts. This may include the next 50 Districts earmarked (to be confirmed
after PPF) and ready to develop and embed the EDCCS based on the capacity
building and mainstreaming efforts delivered in LGCC3 under Project Result 1.




The National Scale-Up Strategy will be complemented by efforts to harness
parallel financing from potential partners and national resources under policies
and funding facilities such as NP2, SCF and SNIF.

those of the NCDD-S and other Steering Group and PMU stakeholders have
significantly increased during the past 10-years since LoCAL was established in
Cambodia. This has resulted in a stronger enabling environment receptive to a
scale-up of the PBCRG as part of LGCC3 and an overall transformational change.




23. EDA project selection criteria for sub-project PBCRG investments

Under LGCC3 the pre-financing PBCRG will be transferred to the District
Administration upon meeting minimum standards. The PBCRG is managed and
monitored by the NCDD-S, and overseen by a Grants Committee, which requires the
District to plan and budget for a menu of eligible local climate risk-informed
investments, or sub-projects. The menu of eligible investments for sub-projects
will be refined during the PPF phase after the Climate Vulnerability Assessment
and Feasibility Study have been conducted. An example of a menu of investments
and indicative costings for adaptation interventions aligned with the climate
specific PBCRG is provided in Annex 3. Each of the targeted 15 Districts in the
LGCC3 project will develop an ‘Enhanced District Climate Change Strategy’
(EDCCS) aligned with a ‘District Investment Programme’ (DIP) to identify local
context-specific climate risks, vulnerable groups, locations and key adaptation
measures by intervention area, specific sub-project type, and size. The NCDD-S
will indicate to the District Administration, to take into account a PBCRG award
when developing its annual plans and budget. Therefore, the District
Administration’s budget will reflect its existing budget commitments to climate
response and the PBCRG transfer for eligible climate-subprojects. The PBCRG for
sub-projects focus on climate-specific standalone funding and top-up existing
District Administration allocations towards resilient and sustainable
development. The PBCRG is therefore ringfenced and traceable through District
planning and budgeting cycles.

four climate change adaptation result areas (see Annex 3: Menu of Eligible
investment):

1. Services for strengthening the climate resilience of vulnerable people,
communities and livelihoods (including planning and capacity building);

2. Services for strengthening climate resilience for health, water and food
security;

3. Climate proofing of infrastructure to protect against climate-related damage
and support adaptation (incremental cost); and

4. Ecosystems and ecosystem services.

decision-making, budgeting and implementation of local adaptation measures in

Assessment (APA) 12-months following disbursement, with the results affecting
future grant levels to the District Administration. The PBCRG therefore offers
additionality and an incentive for good performance at the local government
level.
